newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: RABOBANK HAS TIGHT GRIP ON FOKKER TECHNOLOGY LEASE.
newsitem.headline: RABOBANK HAS TIGHT GRIP ON FOKKER TECHNOLOGY LEASE.

text.p: Dutch Rabobank said the technical knowledge it leased from plane-maker Fokker in 1994 was not automatically for sale if the takeover talks with South Korea's Samsung Aerospace Industries come to a halt.
"The knowledge is there for a reviving Fokker," said a Rabobank spokesman on Wednesday. "We have not put it in the shop-window."
Analysts estimated the value of the knowledge on Fokker it held through technology lease agreements was worth at least 400-600 million guilders.

The cooperative bank received tax benefits after the deal. The Dutch watchdog body on government spending said on Wednesday these considerably exceeded the 412 million guilders that had been injected into the Fokker capital through this transaction.
Rabobank picked up the lease in 1994 as Fokker cast around for ways to raise cash, but a Rabobank spokesman on Wednesday declined to say what the bank had paid for them.
"Rabobank can compensate the costs on the deal with Fokker over some years," said the Rabobank spokesman. "We continue to depreciate this from our balance sheet," he said.

Analysts said Fokker, which went bankrupt in March, was almost stripped to the bones since engineering and services group Stork acquired the profitable maintenance division Fokker Aviation and most staff have left the firm or were made redundant when Fokker went bankrupt.
Since then several possible buyers have been circling Fokker, of which Samsung seemed most keen.
Analysts said the chance that the deal with Samsung would proceed was thin. "It is not an industry any more, it's a few leftovers from a sector," said Andre Mulder of BZW.
Gert Jochems of NIBStrating said the remains of Fokker were only worth "some tens of millions of guilders".
"Rabobank might have something like half a billion guilders in its drawer through the knowledge it leased from Fokker about two years ago," Jochems said.

The Rabobank spokesman declined to say whether Samsung had approached his company over the techno-leases, while analysts said Samsung was expected to apply to Rabobank for the knowledge it leased from plane-maker Fokker NV.
"Why buy some working plants, machines and few of the staff left? The more direct way would be to contact Rabobank to acquire the knowledge (for building aeroplanes)," said one.

Earlier today, Dutch media reported that talks between Samsung and the Dutch government on the revival of bankrupt plane-maker Fokker were foundering on the issue of job security, although Dutch television reported last Sunday that negotiators from Samsung had reached broad agreement on the takeover.
Analysts said the knowledge Rabobank has in stock was related to the 70, 100 and 120-seater aircraft.
